newsitem.title: GERMANY: Iranian envoy warns of "deep crisis" in Bonn ties.
newsitem.headline: Iranian envoy warns of "deep crisis" in Bonn ties.

text.p: Iran's ambassador warned Bonn on Friday of a "deep crisis" in bilateral relations if a court backs prosecutors' accusations that Tehran ordered the 1992 gangland-style killing of three Kurdish dissidents in Berlin.
"If it comes to a conviction, there will be a deep crisis between Bonn and Tehran," Seyen Hosein Mousavian said. "It would be practically impossible to maintain current relations."

The envoy's remarks, published in the Sueddeutsche Zeitung newspaper, came as both Chancellor Helmut Kohl and Iranian President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani intervened to try to stop the spat spiralling out of control.
Kohl said in a letter to Rafsanjani released on Thursday night that Germany had no intention of injuring the religious feelings of the Iranian people and its spiritual leaders.

Rafsanjani said in a prayer sermon on Friday at Tehran University he had received Kohl's letter, commenting: "I hope we will be able to continue our friendship and cooperation with the German government."
Prosecutors have demanded life sentences for the two main suspects in the murder case, an Iranian and a Lebanese man, and last week accused the Tehran leadership of ordering the attack.
The dissidents and their translator were killed in a hail of bullets when gunmen burst into Berlin's "Mykonos" restaurant. The court is expected to announce its verdict in January.
The accusations provoked fury in Iran. Protesters have rallied outside the German embassy several times, throwing eggs and tomatoes and calling for the death of the prosecutors.
Germany, Iran's biggest trading partner, has maintained its "critical dialogue" with Tehran, although Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel now prefers to call it "actively exerting influence".
But there were signs on Friday some members of parliament are growing impatient with the strategy and want tougher action.

"Diplomatic relations must be broken off when prosecutors investigate a case and conclude the Iranian leadership is involved," Wilfried Penner, the chairman of parliament's domestic affairs committee, told the Bild daily.

"We should pull our diplomats out of Tehran as soon as possible because a government which orders and carries out murders inside and outside of Persia is not to be trusted," said Hans-Otto Wilhelm, a member of Kohl's Christian Democrats.
But the chairman of parliament's foreign affairs committee, Karlheinz Hornhues, said he opposed his colleagues' calls.

"We have a situation where Iran is obviously trying hard to reduce the tensions and play down the whole thing," he told SWF Radio. "There's no sense in such a reaction (breaking off relations) when we have a situation like this."
Mousavian moved to distance the Iranian government from the death threats of angry protesters.
"We will only combat the accusations within the framework of German and international law," he said. "Death threats are not the policy of the Iranian government."
